sets.s: My friend should have less sugary drinks in his diet to better protect his teeth.
i: Sugary drinks are the main reason that the friend’s teeth would need protecting.
N
Sugary drinks are implied to be bad for his teeth, but it is not mentioned that they are the leading cause of damaging teeth.
The friend has too many sugary drinks in his diet.
M

He should have less because it is thought to protect his teeth. We’re told what the friend should do to better protect their teeth. By stating that they should have less sugary drinks, we can assume that reducing drinks is necessary and that they have too many.
Consuming too much sugar can be bad for your teeth.
M

If sugary drinks damage teeth, then we can assume that it is the sugar in the drinks that does this, otherwise the passage wouldn’t have stated ‘sugary drinks,’ but ‘drinks’ in general. Also, we will assume that the everyone else’s teeth are susceptible to damage from sugar, just like this person’s friend as nothing is said about them being a special case.

sets.s: The football team requires a better game plan than the one they already have if they want a better chance at winning against their superior rivals.
i: The team’s rivals have a better game plan than they do.
N

The rivals are said to be superior, but this might be due to other factors, and not just better game plans. We can’t make any assumptions on the quality or strength of either team’s game plans as we have no information in the statement to base this on.
The team don’t currently have a good chance at winning against their rivals.
M

The second sentence of the statement suggests that a change must occur for the team to improve their chances of winning, but we’re not told whether their odds of winning are already good nor bad. The rivals are described as ‘superior’, hence we’re automatically convinced to believe that an inferior team have poorer chances of beating their rivals than the rivals have of beating them.
The team cannot win with the current game plan they have.
N
The team would have a better chance of winning with a better game plan, but nothing in the statement can lead us to assume that they have zero chance of winning with their current game plan.

sets.s: The people of New Zealand who took part in ‘The Tree Sitters of Pureora’ protest (1978) were right to do so. The protest was to stop deforestation of the Pureora forest.
i: The protest was a success.
N

The passage says that the protesters were right to do so, not that they were successful. For example, the protest could have failed, the forest was cut down and then the rest of the country could later realise that the protesters were correct.
A lot of the Pureora forest had already been cut down.
N
The passage just says that it was to stop the deforestation of the Pureora forest, it doesn’t mention how much had been cut down.
People protested because they wanted there to be more wildlife.
N
They could have been protesting for any number of reasons, not just for having more wildlife.

sets.s: A franchise usually grows at a much faster rate than a business that is not a franchise. A franchise licenses its trade name and its operating methods to a person or group for a percentage cut of profits earned.
i: A franchise is often better than a non-franchise at expanding a business’s name.
N
The statement says that a franchise usually grows faster than a non-franchise business. But we are not aware of whether it is or is not less profitable than a non-franchise. So assumption not made.
Franchise arrangements can be mutually beneficial to both the main business and the person or group operating it.
M

The benefits we can draw from the statement for running a franchise are that the franchise received a share of the franchisee’s profits. The franchisee benefits from being able to use the franchise’s trade name, and the licence to conduct business in the same way as the franchise. The franchisee is also more likely to grow at a faster rate than if they hadn’t set up as a franchisee. Both parties benefit, so it is a safe assumption that a franchise arrangement is mutually beneficial.
A trade name is valued.
M
An assumption can easily be made that a trade name is valued. The value of the trade name is equivalent to a percentage of the profits, which a franchisee believes is worth paying.
